Closes #2885.

Create the possibility to provide a RegExp to the `addContentTypeParser` API.

```js
fastify.addContentTypeParser(/^image\/.*/, function (request, payload, done) {
  imageParser(payload, function (err, body) {
    done(err, body)
  })
})
```

In the current implementation, fastify first tries to match a content-type parser with a string value before trying to find a matching RegExp.
Additionally, I updated the documentation to demonstrate the user in which order fastify searches for a matching content type parser.
I can provide benchmark results if necessary.

issue_context.title: Support RegExp for the addContentTypeParser API
issue_context.body:
<!--
Before you submit an issue we recommend you visit [Fastify Help](https://github.com/fastify/help) and ask any questions you have or mention any problems you've had getting started with Fastify.

**Please read this entire template before posting any issue. If you ignore these instructions
and post an issue here that does not follow the instructions, your issue might be closed,
locked, and assigned the `missing discussion` label.**
-->

## 🚀 Feature Proposal

Support `RegExp` for the `addContentTypeParser` API.

## Motivation

Currently, you need to add a new content type parser for each new content type you use. So you have to add 2 parsers if you use the content types `application/vnd.user+json` and `application/vnd.book+json`, even though both are valid JSON objects and could use the same content type parser. This could be possible if the `addContentTypeParser` API supported `RegExp` in addition to string values.

## Example

```javascript
fastify.addContentTypeParser(/s*\+json$/, { parseAs: "string" }, function (req, body, done) {
  try {
    var json = JSON.parse(body)
    done(null, json)
  } catch (err) {
    err.statusCode = 400
    done(err, undefined)
  }
})
```
comments: Would you like to send a Pull Request to address this issue? Remember to add unit tests.
Yes, I will send a PR as soon as I am done.
`application/jso` looks like a typo? Where does this happen?

It was just an example to show the current behaviour of the contentTypeParser.
Another and more understandable example:

```javascript
const app: FastifyInstance = fastify( options );

app.addContentTypeParser( 'application/vnd.custom+xml', { parseAs: "string" }, (request, body, done) => {} )

app.addContentTypeParser( 'application/vnd.custom', { parseAs: "string" }, (request, body, done) => {} )
```
In this example the first contentTypeParser function will never be called, because the second one also matches the first content type. To achieve the desired behaviour the user have to make the `addContentTypeParser` calls in the right order.
Like this:

```javascript
const app: FastifyInstance = fastify( options );

app.addContentTypeParser( 'application/vnd.custom', { parseAs: "string" }, (request, body, done) => {} )

app.addContentTypeParser( 'application/vnd.custom+xml', { parseAs: "string" }, (request, body, done) => {} )
```

So my question is: Should we leave the responsibility to the user to call the API in the correct order or should Fastify take care of that?

> So my question is: Should we leave the responsibility to the user to call the API in the correct order or should Fastify take care of that?

I think the responsibility is on the user.
Is this behavior pointed out somewhere in the docs?
Currently not. I will update the documentation accordingly since I need to change it anyway to add the regex support.
